newsitem.title: USA: Dakota Mining has definitive agreement to acquire USMX.
newsitem.headline: Dakota Mining has definitive agreement to acquire USMX.

text.p: USMX Inc. said Friday it has signed a definitive agreement to be acquired by Dakota Mining Corp., a Canadian-based mining company, in a stock deal valued at about $22.3 million.
The combined company will be a mid-sized gold producer with production of some 140,000 ounces annually commencing in 1997, growing to 200,000 ounces in 1998, USMX said.

Dakota, based in Vancouver, British Columbia, will offer one common share for every 1.1 shares of USMX's stock. USMX has 16.2 million common shares outstanding, while Dakota has 35.5 million shares outstanding.
USMX will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Dakota.
The merger is subject to approval by the Toronto Stock Exchange, regulators and shareholders and creditors of both companies.
Dakota's board will consist of four USMX appointees, including one designated by USMX's largest stockholder, Pegasus Gold Inc., and five Dakota appointees.
USMX, based in Denver, operates mineral properties in North and Latin America.
Dakota's stock was unchange at $1.50 on the American Stock Exchange in late trading. USMX edged down 9 cents to $1.34 on Nasdaq.
